fluff.overview: The Mao-Heng Charioteer is a light wheeled patrol vehicle commissioned in 2797 by Chancellor Sandol Quinn of the Capellan Confederation. Designed exclusively for the Palace Guard on Sian, the Mao-Heng was intended as a law enforcement cruiser capable of navigating urban streets under fossil fuel power. Despite its sleek exterior, the vehicle earned a reputation for sluggish handling and underwhelming performance almost immediately after entering service. Production was extremely limited, with fewer than two thousand units completed before the line was shut down. The design languished in obscurity for over two centuries before academic researchers revived it as a modernized police cruiser in the mid-thirty-first century.
fluff.capabilities:
The Mao-Heng Charioteer is a ten-ton wheeled support vehicle powered by an internal combustion engine. Its top speed of just sixty kilometers per hour makes it one of the slowest patrol vehicles ever fielded, a shortcoming that proved a constant liability during urban policing operations. The vehicle carries no weapons whatsoever, relying entirely on its crew and any embarked personnel to provide armed response. Eight passenger seats allow it to function as a personnel transport for small security details or prisoner transfers, with an additional four hundred kilograms of rear-mounted cargo space for equipment or evidence storage.

Protective armor is minimal, rated at BAR 4, offering only modest resistance to small arms fire and virtually no protection against military-grade weaponry. The two-person crew consists of enlisted, non-rated personnel, reflecting the vehicle's purely civilian law enforcement role. While the Mao-Heng's low operating costs and simple maintenance requirements offered some practical advantages for cash-strapped planetary constabularies, these benefits could not offset its fundamental shortcomings in speed and survivability.
fluff.deployment: The (Original) designation refers to the initial Mao-Heng Charioteer as produced from 2797 to 2799 under Chancellor Quinn's patronage. This variant carries the Obsolete design quirk for the period of 2801 through 3043, reflecting the two-century gap between the cancellation of first-run production and the vehicle's revival as a modernized police cruiser. The original production run saw exclusive deployment with the Palace Guard and Capellan Hussars on Sian, where the vehicles served in an urban law enforcement capacity until the last unit was retired in 2834.
fluff.history:
In early 2797, Chancellor Sandol Quinn personally established the requirements for a new patrol vehicle to serve the Palace Guard on Sian. The specifications called for a wheeled design powered by fossil fuels with a minimum speed of sixty kilometers per hour. Quinn's procurement process attracted considerable controversy, as rumors persisted that wealthy associates with interests in the fossil fuel mining industry had influenced the contract requirements. Multiple companies submitted entries, and despite several more promising candidates, the sleek but sluggish Mao-Heng was selected.

Initial production lasted fewer than two years, yielding less than two thousand vehicles before political upheaval ended the program. When Dame Ilsa Liao came of age in 2801, Quinn abdicated his stewardship of the throne in favor of the rightful Liao heir. Shortly thereafter, production of the Mao-Heng was suspended and eventually cancelled entirely.

For several years afterward, the remaining Mao-Hengs continued to patrol the streets of Sian under the fanatically loyal Capellan Hussars. The vehicles developed a mixed reputation during this period. The most notorious example was Patrol 13, which gained infamy beginning in July 2809 after its fifth consecutive month of being towed away from armed confrontations with Triad malcontents. Historians on Purvo later claimed the vehicle received numerous commendations, though irregularities in their records suggest the awards reflected the uncommon valor of the Hussars assigned to the unlucky cruiser rather than any merit of the vehicle itself. Patrol 13 was the last Mao-Heng decommissioned, finally retired in 2834 and purchased by Duke Jian Kao of Purvo for his personal collection.

The Mao-Heng remained forgotten for over two centuries until 3042, when a team of student researchers led by Professor George Sheng at the Sian Regional Training Center selected the design as a graduation project. Their internally reworked prototype performed well enough that the Ministry of Transportation took notice. Within six months, a contract was awarded to Professor Sheng to oversee construction of a new production line featuring the modernized Mao-Heng. The vehicle was once again designated as a law enforcement standard issue, and production as a police cruiser resumed with plans for it to replace older patrol vehicles across Capellan worlds.
